Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Aether Clean Energy Corp. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants may register for questions by pressing star then one on their touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aether Clean Energy Corp.'s results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Thornton, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Development Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Aether Clean Energy Corp. delivered a solid performance in the Q2 2024, driven by strong execution and growing demand for our renewable energy solutions. We are making significant progress on our strategic priorities, including expanding our project pipeline, enhancing our technological capabilities, and strengthening our partnerships.

I'd like to highlight four key aspects of our performance this quarter.

First, on our capacity addition guidance and pipeline targets. As we continue to execute on our leadership position in the global renewables market, this remains the cornerstone of our growth story, underpinned by the accelerating energy transition, supportive policy tailwinds like the US Inflation Reduction Act's PTC and ITC extensions, Europe's REPowerEU targets, and emerging markets' net-zero pledges.

Let's recap our installed base. As of June 30th, we stand at 18.2 GW of operational capacity across our portfolio—up 25% year-over-year. This includes 12.4 GWdc of utility-scale solar PV, 4.8 GW of onshore wind, 0.7 GW of offshore wind, and 0.3 GWh of co-located battery energy storage systems. Our fleet continues to deliver strong performance, with a year-to-date capacity factor of 28% for solar—bolstered by our shift to high-efficiency heterojunction and TOPCon modules averaging 22.5% efficiency—and 38% for wind assets leveraging longer blades and taller hubs.

Turning to full-year 2024 capacity addition guidance, we are reaffirming our target of 4.5 to 5.0 GW of net new additions, implying a 25-28% growth on our starting base. We've already achieved 2.1 GW in the first half, including the 650 MWdc SunForge solar project in Texas, which reached commercial operation in Q2 under a 15-year PPA with ERCOT load-serving entities at an attractive $28/MWh all-in PPA price. The back half of the year will see the lion's share: 1.2 GWdc from three solar-plus-storage hybrids in California under the state's SB 100 mandate, featuring 400 MWh/200 MW 4-hour BESS utilizing CATL's latest LFP cells for enhanced dispatchability. Additionally, 800 MW of onshore wind in the US Midwest—partnering with Vestas for 5.X platforms—and our first 150 MW offshore phase in the US Northeast, leveraging GE Haliade-X turbines amid BOEM's accelerated permitting under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.

By technology, solar remains our growth engine at about 65% of additions, or 3.0 GWdc, driven by module costs down 15% YoY to $0.22/Wdc amid PERC-to-TOPCon transitions and US domestic content bonuses under IRA Section 45X, which we're capturing at 10-12% adder on qualifying projects. Wind contributes 25%, or 1.1 GW, with BESS ramping to 10%, or 0.45 GWh, as we prioritize firming to meet PJM and CAISO ancillary service demands.

For 2025 guidance, we're introducing a target of 6.0 to 7.0 GW additions—our strongest yet—fueled by $2.5 billion in incremental PPAs signed YTD, including corporate offtakes from tech giants like a hyperscaler counterpart to Google's 860 MW deal earlier this year. This reflects a 30-40% CAGR through 2027, outpacing the IEA's projected 25% global renewables capacity growth.

On our development pipeline, we maintain the industry's most robust and derisked queue at 62 GW advanced-stage projects, from shovel-ready to notice to proceed, and 145 GW early-stage, from greenfield to permitting. This positions us for 20+ GW annual additions by 2028, with a 3x conversion multiple from advanced to commercial operation date.

Regionally, the US represents 55% of the pipeline, or 105 GW total, with 35 GW advanced, targeting IRA-optimized solar plus BESS in the Southwest, like a 2 GW queue interconnection with APS, and wind repowers in the Plains. Permitting tailwinds from FAST-41 and our 85% success rate on FERC queues give us confidence in 8 GW COD in 2025-26. Europe is 25%, or 50 GW, with 15 GW advanced, focused on offshore wind auctions in the UK North Sea, CfD AR6 targeting 4 GW Hinkley-adjacent, and hybrid parks in Iberia with 1.2 GW electrolyzer integration for green hydrogen under IPCEI Hy2Use. Grid bottlenecks persist, but our €500M investment in private interconnectors mitigates this. Asia-Pacific is 15%, or 35 GW, with 8 GW advanced in India, SEC I-approved 5 GW solar, and Australia, 1 GW VRE under ERF auctions, capitalizing on PLI scheme incentives and AEMO's ISP roadmap for 82 GW renewables by 2030. Emerging and LatAm is 5%, or 17 GW, with early traction in Brazil's hybrid auctions and Chile's 24/7 carbon-free pilots.

Strategically, we're accelerating technical initiatives to de-risk and upscale: first, co-location mandates—90% of new solar and wind now paired with BESS at 1:4 DC:AC ratios, targeting 95%+ capture rates; second, floating offshore wind pilots, 500 MW pipeline off California, partnering with Equinor's Hywind tech; third, AI-driven operations and maintenance via our Nexus platform, boosting annual energy production by 5-7% through predictive curtailment avoidance; fourth, supply chain localization—securing 70% US/EU-sourced modules and blades to lock in IRA transferability monetization at 90% of value.

Challenges remain: supply chain inflation persists at 5-8% for balance-of-system components, permitting delays average 18 months versus our 12-month target, and interconnection queues exceed 2 TW globally per LBNL data. We've countered with $1.2B in M&A YTD, including a carve-out from Invenergy's 3 GW Midwest portfolio, and hedging 80% of turbine deliveries.

In summary, our capacity guidance and pipeline underscore a path to 50 GW operational by 2027, with contracted backlog covering 85% of the next three years at IRRs north of 12%. This derisks our FCF conversion to 90%+ and supports our progressive dividend policy.

Second, on tax equity financing and project-level financing. These mechanisms remain the bedrock of our capital stack in the renewable energy sector, enabling us to scale our portfolio of utility-scale solar, wind, and hybrid battery storage projects while optimizing our balance sheet and delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for shareholders.

Tax equity financing has been a game-changer for Aether Clean Energy Corp., particularly in the post-IRA landscape. For those less familiar, it involves partnering with institutional investors—typically large banks, insurance companies, or yieldcos—who have substantial taxable income and appetite for the Investment Tax Credit under Section 48 or the Production Tax Credit under Section 45. In a typical partnership flip structure, the tax equity investor contributes 30-40% of a project's capital cost in exchange for the lion's share of ITC/PTC benefits and cash distributions until they achieve a target IRR—often in the 8-10% range post-IRA adders—after which control flips back to us as the sponsor.

In Q2, we closed two marquee tax equity facilities totaling $725 million. The first was a $450 million partnership with US Bancorp for our 250 MW Desert Bloom solar-plus-storage project in Riverside County, California. This bifacial PERC module array, paired with 100 MWh of Tesla Megapack storage, qualifies for the full 70% ITC adder under the domestic content and energy community bonuses from the Inflation Reduction Act. Tax equity covered 35% of the $1.3 billion capex, with yields for our partner hitting 9.2% on a levered basis. Commercial operations are on track for Q4 2024, backed by a 20-year PPA with Southern California Edison at an all-in fixed price of $42/MWh, delivering an LCOE of $28/MWh—competitive even in a high-interest-rate environment.

Our second closing was $275 million with JPMorgan Chase for a 150 MW onshore wind farm in Texas' ERCOT market, utilizing Vestas V150-4.2 MW turbines with 20% capacity factor uplift from our proprietary wake steering tech. Here, PTCs at $27/MWh base plus 10% adder drove a 38% tax equity contribution to the $850 million project cost. We've seen tax equity demand surge 25% YoY across our pipeline, fueled by IRA transferability provisions allowing monetization to third parties, which has broadened our investor pool beyond traditional players like Wells Fargo and KeyBanc to include newcomers like PGIM and MetLife.

Regionally, U.S. tax equity remains dominant—accounting for 65% of our FY24 financings—but we're expanding into Europe via yieldcos like Ørsted and Green Investment Group, leveraging the EU's Renewable Energy Directive III for similar PTC-like mechanisms. In APAC, Australia's Large-scale Generation Certificates are opening doors, though yields are compressing to 7-8% amid falling module prices from Chinese Tier 1s like Longi and Jinko.

Shifting to project-level financing, this is our non-recourse debt layer, secured solely by project assets, PPAs, and offtake contracts—keeping it off our corporate balance sheet and preserving liquidity. We typically layer it atop tax equity and our 20-25% sponsor equity, targeting 50-60% advance rates with debt tenors of 15-18 years.

Q2 highlights include a $1.2 billion construction-to-term loan from a syndicate led by MUFG and Rabobank for our 400 MW SunForge portfolio in the PJM market—three projects with Nextracker single-axis systems and 50 MWh BESS hybrids. This replaced our prior $900 million construction facility at Libor + 175 bps, refinancing into term debt at SOFR + 195 bps with a 1.45x DSCR covenant and 18-year amortizing schedule. The all-in cost? 5.8% blended, up 50 bps from last year due to Fed hikes, but mitigated by our 12% hedge on floating portions.

We've also executed back-leverage facilities, like the $300 million holdco loan against our stabilized 1.2 GW operating assets, at 4.75% fixed via Allianz, funding dividends and growth capex. Trends here show construction spreads widening to 250-300 bps over Treasuries amid bank scrutiny post-SVB, but our 98% fleet uptime and A-rated PPAs with investment-grade counterparties like Google and Microsoft keep pricing tight.

Strategically, these tools interplay seamlessly: tax equity de-risks upfront via credits, project debt provides cheap leverage on predictable cash flows, and we retain 60-70% upside post-flip. With interest rates peaking, we're front-loading fixed-rate term debt—$3.5 billion queued for H2—and exploring NAV facilities against our 5 GW development pipeline. IRA-driven adder stacking has boosted unlevered IRRs to 9-11%, attracting $15 billion in committed facilities from our core partners.

Looking ahead, we expect $2-2.5 billion in tax equity closings by YE24, with project finance matching that pace, fully funding our build program. This positions Aether Clean Energy Corp. for 15-20% FCF growth in 2025, even as module prices dip 15% QoQ.

Third, on new PPAs secured and average PPA price. PPAs remain the bedrock of our contracted revenue backlog, providing long-term visibility and de-risking our 15 GW development pipeline across utility-scale solar, wind-plus-storage hybrids, and emerging clean tech like long-duration energy storage.

In Q2, we announced five new PPAs totaling 1.2 GW of capacity, bringing our total contracted backlog to 8.4 GW—up 25% year-over-year and representing over 55% of our five-year buildout target. These agreements span three regions: the US Southwest, ERCOT in Texas, and our growing European footprint in Spain. The counterparties are a who's who of high-credit, sustainability-focused buyers: two hyperscale tech giants—one akin to Microsoft for 450 MW—a major retail conglomerate like Walmart for 300 MW, a leading California utility similar to PG&E for 250 MW, and a European industrial off-taker in the chemicals sector for 200 MW.

Breaking it down project-by-project: Our Desert Bloom Solar + Storage project in Arizona is a 450 MWdc bifacial solar array paired with 150 MWh of front-of-the-meter BESS, using N-type TOPCon modules from Longi and single-axis trackers from Nextracker. This 15-year PPA with the hyperscaler starts at an all-in fixed price of $36/MWh, escalating 2% annually for inflation protection, with built-in availability guarantees and shapeable dispatch rights for grid services. COD targeted for Q4 2026.

In ERCOT, the Lone Star Wind Hybrid—400 MW of IEC Class III turbines from Vestas integrated with 200 MW/800 MWh flow battery storage from our partner Ambri—secured a 12-year PPA at $42/MWh with the retail major. This one's merchant-upside hybrid: base PPA covers 80% of output, with the remainder exposed to ERCOT's real-time nodal pricing, which averaged $55/MWh last quarter amid heatwave-driven scarcity.

California's Pacific Ridge Solar, 250 MWac with our proprietary perovskite tandem modules achieving 25%+ efficiency in pilot—locked in with the utility at $48/MWh over 20 years, including LCFS credits and a carbon adder tied to California's cap-and-trade.

And in Spain, under REPowerEU momentum, our 200 MW Andalusia Agri-PV project—agrivoltaics with sheep grazing for dual-use land optimization—at €32/MWh, about $35/MWh, with the industrial buyer, a 10-year deal with CFD-like revenue floors.

These wins aren't just volume; they're strategically calibrated. Average tenor is 14 years, with 95% investment-grade counterparties, diversifying us beyond pure utilities—hyperscalers now represent 28% of backlog, up from 15% last year, capitalizing on their 24/7 carbon-free mandates and the AI/data center power crunch projected by EIA to add 45 GW US demand by 2030.

Our blended fleet-wide average PPA price stands at $38/MWh as of Q2 end—down 8% YoY from $41/MWh, aligning with industry benchmarks from NREL's Q1 2024 Utility-Scale PV report showing median solar PPAs at $37/MWh nationally. This compression reflects three tailwinds we've aggressively pursued: technology-driven cost deflation, with LCOE for our utility-scale solar dropped to $24/MWh—a 15% YoY decline—thanks to 30% BoS reductions from larger 600W+ modules, AI-optimized tracker algorithms cutting soiling losses by 12%, and economies from our 2 GW module offtake with JinkoSolar. Wind hybrids benefit from 10 MW-class turbines, pushing hub heights to 150m for +20% capacity factors.

Supply chain mastery: fixed-price EPC contracts locked in Q3 '23 shielded us from 5-7% steel/polysilicon volatility, unlike some peers reporting 10%+ overruns. Our US content exceeds 60% under IRA guidelines, unlocking $0.12/kWh PTC adders—boosting effective PPA yields to $50/MWh on federal tax equity deals.

Market dynamics: US Southwest PPAs averaged $35/MWh, down 12% YoY per WoodMac, pressured by 200 GW queued solar but buoyed by IRA ITC transferability. ERCOT's hybrid pricing holds a 20% premium at $45/MWh due to scarcity pricing—our exposure here hedges volume risk. Europe, post-Ukraine, sees €30-35/MWh floors from auctions, with Spain's 7 GW 2024 tender underscoring oversupply risks we're mitigating via storage collars.

While headline $/MWh dips, our PPA value metric—net revenue per MWh after O&M/taxes—rose 5% to $32/MWh, driven by 98% uptime via digital twins and drone-based IV curve analytics. We've embedded ESG escalators in 40% of new deals, tying 1-2% annual bumps to Scope 2 reductions verified by RE100 standards.

Looking forward, our 5 GW PPA pipeline—60% utility-scale solar-plus-storage—targets Q3/Q4 closings at $37/MWh blended, with 70% US exposure leveraging IRA's $369B tailwinds. Risks like transmission delays in CAISO, with MISO-style queues hit 2-year averages, and European auction fatigue are countered with 500 MW shovel-ready brownfield sites and PPAs with take-or-pay merchant collars.

These new PPAs fortify our $15B revenue backlog—85% fixed-price—delivering 12-14% unlevered IRR at current pricing, with upside from $100B+ in ancillary services markets.

Fourth, on storage deployment and hybrid project updates. Energy storage—primarily through our battery energy storage systems, or BESS—is pivotal for unlocking the full value of renewables by addressing intermittency, enabling dispatchable power, and capturing high-margin ancillary services. Our hybrid projects, which co-locate solar PV, onshore wind, or even emerging green hydrogen assets with storage, are scaling rapidly, driven by falling LCOE for lithium-iron-phosphate batteries—now down 22% year-over-year per BloombergNEF's latest Q2 report—and supportive policies like the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act's ITC adder for standalone storage at 30-50%.

In Q2, we achieved first-energy from our Pioneer Valley BESS project in ERCOT, Texas—a 200 MW / 800 MWh AC-coupled system utilizing Tesla Megapack 2XL units. This brings our total deployed storage capacity to 1.2 GW / 4.8 GWh year-to-date, up 45% from Q2 2023, and positions us as a top-5 independent power producer in U.S. wholesale storage per S&P Global Platts rankings. Utilization hit 85% in Pioneer Valley, generating $18 million in revenue at an average arbitrage spread of $150/MWh during peak summer demand, supplemented by $5.2 million from ERCOT's real-time co-optimization for frequency response and contingency reserves. Round-trip efficiency stands at 94.2%, benefiting from our proprietary AI-driven battery management system that optimizes charge/discharge cycles using machine learning algorithms trained on 5+ years of CAISO and ERCOT data.

Our storage pipeline remains robust at 6.2 GW / 25 GWh through 2027, with 70% contracted under long-term PPAs or capacity agreements. Notable progress includes nearing COD for the 150 MW / 600 MWh Sunland Hybrid in California's CAISO market, DC-coupled to our adjacent 400 MWdc solar farm. This project is already pre-qualified for the 2025 Capacity Performance auction, where storage cleared at record $400/kW-year levels. Construction is underway on 300 MW / 1.2 GWh in Australia's NEM, leveraging the Clean Energy Finance Corporation's $500 million debt facility. Here, we're stacking revenue from FCAS markets, yielding 25% EBITDA margins, amid AEMO's forecast of 5 GW storage additions by FY26 to manage rooftop solar saturation.

Regionally, U.S. operations drove 60% of Q2 storage EBITDA at 65% margins, up from 55% last year, thanks to IRA-driven tax equity partnerships—we closed $450 million with a major bank syndicate in May. In Europe, our 100 MW / 400 MWh Nordic Flex project in the UK's Balancing Mechanism is performing ahead of plan, capturing £50/MWh spreads during wind lulls, while navigating Ofgem's Cap and Floor regime. Challenges persist in Germany, where EEG surcharge reforms have slowed auctions, but our 80 MWdc / 40 MW-4hr hybrid bid won 90% strike price coverage in the latest Bundesnetzagentur round.

Hybrids now represent 55% of our development pipeline—up from 35% in 2023—as co-location reduces interconnection queues by 40% and boosts project IRRs to 12-14% versus 9-11% for standalone renewables. Q2 milestones include full commercial ops at Horizon Winds + Store, a 250 MW onshore wind + 100 MW / 400 MWh BESS hybrid in PJM. Wind curtailment dropped 65% post-storage integration, unlocking $22 million annualized revenue uplift through energy arbitrage and RPM capacity payments at $130/kW-year. We're using GE Vernova's 6.0 MW turbines paired with Fluence Cube OS for grid-forming inverters, enabling black-start capabilities critical for PJM's evolving ride-through standards. FID achieved on SolarForge Hybrid in India’s SECI auction: 500 MWdc fixed-tilt solar + 200 MW / 800 MWh storage, at a record-low blended tariff of INR 2.60/kWh, or $0.031. This leverages SECI's deviation settlement matrix and our LFP packs from CATL, with VRE forecasting via IBM Watson integration to hit 28% capacity factor.

Strategically, we're accelerating hybrids to front-run global trends: BNEF projects 140 GW of new storage additions in 2024, with hybrids comprising 40%, fueled by China's dominance in LFP supply chains, prices at $95/kWh, and U.S. manufacturing credits under the IRA. We've inked a 2 GWh offtake with Sungrow for next-gen liquid-cooled systems, targeting 96% RTE and 4-hour duration to compete in MISO's emerging hybrid markets. M&A-wise, we're eyeing tuck-ins like the 500 MW development platform from a distressed developer in the NEM, funded via our $1.2 billion green bond issuance at 4.25% yield.

Looking forward, we guide 1.8 GW / 7.2 GWh total storage deployments for FY24, up 50% YoY, with hybrids contributing $300 million in contracted revenue backlog growth. Storage-adjusted EBITDA margins expand to 62-65%, supported by our 20% cost reduction initiative via vertical integration into cell manufacturing pilots.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Thornton to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Thornton:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. As Dr. Vasquez mentioned, we had a strong financial performance in the Q2 2024. Our revenue was $1.25 billion, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by increased project commissioning and higher energy production across our portfolio. Our gross margin was 44%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $285 million, primarily due to increased investments in research and development and sales and marketing. Our net income was $210 million, or $1.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $2.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue of $5.2 to $5.6 billion and earnings per share of $7.50 to $8.00.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Dr. Vasquez for closing remarks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Michael. In closing, I am confident that Aether Clean Energy Corp. is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you have a question at this time, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Lisa Chen with GreenCapital Partners. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of your new perovskite tandem modules on your project economics?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question, Lisa. Our perovskite tandem modules, as highlighted in projects like Pacific Ridge Solar, are achieving over 25% efficiency in pilots, which directly lowers LCOE by about 15-20% compared to standard TOPCon. This translates to higher IRRs, around 2-3 points uplift, and better PPA competitiveness, allowing us to bid more aggressively in auctions while maintaining margins above 12%. We've seen this play out in our recent California wins, where the efficiency gains offset any premium module costs through reduced land and BoS expenses.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with EcoInvest Advisors. Please go ahead.

David Ruiz:
What are your expectations for grid connection timelines for your upcoming projects?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Excellent question, David. We're optimistic about timelines shortening due to policy tailwinds like FAST-41 in the US, where our 85% FERC queue success rate has us on track for 12-18 month averages versus historical delays. In Europe, our private interconnector investments are mitigating grid bottlenecks, targeting NTP to COD in under 24 months for UK and Iberian hybrids. For our 62 GW advanced pipeline, we're prioritizing shovel-ready sites with existing queues, expecting 8 GW in US CODs for 2025-26, with overall permitting averaging 18 months—still a challenge, but countered by M&A and hedging.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, there appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Dr. Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Aether Clean Energy Corp. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
